pr_title: Fix a bunch of spelling errors across the project
pr_body:
Generated by https://github.com/jsoref/spelling `f`; to maintain your repo, please consider `fchurn`

I generally try to ignore upstream bits. I've accidentally included some items from the `deps/` directory. I expect someone will give me a list of items to drop, I'm happy to drop whole files/directories, or to split the PR into multiple items (E.g. comments/locals/public).

Closes #4294
pr_comments: Wow I like it, but it's going to take me some time to review this. I'll get back around to it.

> @j4james: most of the builds finished ✔️ , but one was marked as ❌ (it appears to have been canceled) and one with ❕ (it also appears to have been canceled). Is this my fault? Is there something I'm supposed to do about them? -- Also, why the discrepancy, if the cause is a timeout in both cases, shouldn't the status be the same for both cases?

I suspect it's not your fault. I couldn't see an actual compile error anywhere. I know the CI build does fail from time to time for reasons unrelated to the code, and usually when that happens one of the MS devs will ask the bot to rebuild. But you can also force a rebuild just by committing again, which you're going to have to do now anyway to rebase (or merge) with the master branch.
@j4james: As you're happy w/ rebase, I'm quite happy to rebase; rebased. (This dropped the `dep/` directory -- I'll fix those repos eventually.)

@jsoref I see the build failed again, but I'm still fairly certain this is not your fault. It's just timed out while running the unit tests, which I've seen happen many times before (I had the same problem in a PR of my own last night). I think the build bot is just having a bad day. Sooner or later someone from MS will likely sort it out.
I've been having a run of bad luck w/ CI systems recently.

> Generated by [jsoref/spelling](https://github.com/jsoref/spelling) `f`; to maintain your repo, please consider `fchurn`

@jsoref, is there a way we can run this as a part of our CI and make it fail on a typo like the clang-tidy style rules do?

@miniksa : yes, for an example of this integration, see: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/master/.ci/test-spelling-unknown-words.sh 

Note: You also need to pick a dictionary. (For licensing reasons, I don't host my own.)

Ideally you want some sort of bucket which stores your previous set of whitelisted words. For checkstyle, that's: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/master/.ci/jsoref-spellchecker/whitelist.words

The right place to store the whitelist is probably a bucket (AWS S3/Azure Blob Storage/GCloud Bucket) -- You don't really want to version the whitelist in the repo as it's a large ever changing file that your users don't actually care about.

I haven't written that code yet (I need to do it for my employer's project).

>  whole fies/directories, 

files

Heheheh...

Also

> I've accidentally included some items from the `deps/` directory.

Be sure you leave those out, for the most part. They come from somewhere else. If you want to make a list of the dependencies that have spelling errors, we can file issues to get them fixed upstream and in here at the same time.

> @miniksa : yes, for an example of this integration, see: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/master/.ci/test-spelling-unknown-words.sh [](/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/HEAD@{2020-02-04T17:50:23Z}/.ci/test-spelling-unknown-words.sh)

For checkstyle, that's: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/master/.ci/jsoref-spellchecker/whitelist.words [](/checkstyle/checkstyle/blob/HEAD@{2020-02-04T17:50:23Z}/.ci/jsoref-spellchecker/whitelist.words)
> 
> The right place to store the whitelist is probably a bucket (AWS S3/Azure Blob Storage/GCloud Bucket) -- You don't really want to version the whitelist in the repo as it's a large ever changing file that your users don't actually care about.
> 
> I haven't written that code yet (I need to do it for my employer's project).

Hm, OK. 

We have a bucket in the form of the bucket we use to store our NuGet packages. We could keep a list there.

We would also need to adapt your BASH script to likely a PowerShell one as that's what we'd have to run in the Windows Server CI.

As for a dictionary, maybe we can use one that's installed with Visual Studio? I'd bet there's one in there somewhere and it'll already be on the build agents.

Let's capture this stuff into another work item.

I think at this point I've successfully dropped `deps/` unless there are similar things hiding elsewhere.

I can resurrect older versions of my changes to identify the things that could use fixing later once this is merged.

I won't have any time to work on this until tonight. (It looks like it's dropping 
53f3966, rebasing, and resolving merge conflicts.)

review_comments: It's possible this is an API of sorts.
Nnnnn. @amit-msft, does this mess up reporting if we correct the typo? Or can you glue the two together on the back-end?
I'm fairly certain this is a correct fix... There's no sign of the string I'm changing.
Ugh. This was my fault. It was App --> AppLogic in an overzealous find/replace. I thought I fixed them all. So yeah. `Apply` is the correct revert.
Man I really need to learn how to spell `indices`.
Fwiw, it is a commonly corrupted word. (Although I haven't seen it much recently, it's definitely something I correct often enough.)
This was imported from somewhere, but it's fine to fix the typo.
Looks like it came out of `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2019\Enterprise\VC\Auxiliary\VS\include\CppCoreCheck\warnings.h` but the typo looks fixed at least of VS 16.4.4 on my system.
Other variables in this file use camelCase (such as `readBack`).
I think the author was trying to avoid it looking like the hungarian notation for "boolean Button" as `bButton`. But it's a test, so I don't mind either way.
